content.title: About
content.content: Kohlrabi is an edible stem vegetable from the Brassicaceae family, related to cabbage, broccoli and radish. Cooked kohlrabi has a tender, mildly sweet flavor and a crisp texture. It can be boiled, stewed, roasted, or steamed.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kohlrabi was known to the ancient Romans and used as a vegetable in Mediterranean cuisine.
The edible part is the swollen stem, not a root like most root vegetables.
Vitamin C content in kohlrabi exceeds that of oranges.
Kohlrabi comes in green and purple varieties; the color depends on the cultivar.
In Japan, kohlrabi is often served thinly sliced and pickled (tsukudani).

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium contributes to normal heart and muscle function.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Cooked kohlrabi fits well into calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Flavonoids and glucosinolates help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Like other cruciferous vegetables, kohlrabi can cause gas in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Thyroid interaction
items.content: Glucosinolates may affect thyroid function when consumed in excess.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience an allergic reaction to kohlrabi.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Kohlrabi can be boiled until tender and added to soups, stews, or casseroles. It also works well sliced thin and quickly sautéed with olive oil and spices. Raw slices are suitable for salads, but the cooked version is milder and more aromatic.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh kohlrabi in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a plastic bag, for up to 1 week. Cooked kohlrabi should be kept in an airtight container in the fridge and consumed within 3‑4 days.
